turns.prompt_text: I am playing legend of Zelda breath of the wild guy in a major test of strength I have a pretty good inventory Attached 1 file. - 325127e1-ee2e-42aa-bfb5-9a34c2ec1fe9
turns.response_html:
You are in a great position to take down the Major Test of Strength Guardian Scout IV. Based on the file 325127e1-ee2e-42aa-bfb5-9a34c2ec1fe9, you are equipped with an Ancient Battle Axe+ (45 Damage), which is perfect for this fight. Because it is an ancient/guardian archetype weapon, it naturally deals a 30% damage bonus against Guardian Scouts.

Here is a breakdown of how to handle each phase of the fight like a pro:

Phase 1: Melee & Spin Attacks

  • Circle Strafe: Keep locked on with ZL. The Guardian Scout will strike with its weapons; simply walk or hop in a circle around it to dodge, then strike its back while it recovers.
  • The Spinning Rush: When the Scout leaps backward and extends its weapons, it is preparing to spin-charge at you.
    • The Easy Counter: Hide behind one of the stone pillars in the arena. If the Scout rams into a pillar, it will stun itself, giving you an opening to unleash a massive combo with your Ancient Battle Axe+.
    • Rune Options: If there are no pillars (or they break), use Cryonis (if there is water on the floor) or Magnesis (if there are metal blocks in the floor) to create an artificial barrier to stop its charge. You can also freeze it mid-spin using Stasis+.

Phase 2: The Laser Circle (Around 50% HP)

  • Ride the Wind: The Scout will hunder down and spin a wide laser beam around the room, which creates a massive updraft.
  • Bullet Time: Pull out your paraglider to ride the updraft into the sky. Drop down, draw your bow to enter slow-motion "bullet time," and fire an arrow straight into its glowing blue eye. A headshot will instantly cancel the attack and stun it on the ground.

Phase 3: The Death Laser (Below 20% HP)

  • The Charging Phase: The Scout will stand still, turn red, and lock a targeting laser onto you while charging up a massive 4-shot blast.
  • Go All Out: This is your "spin to win" window. Run right up to it, hold down your attack button to spin with your Ancient Battle Axe+, and dish out as much damage as possible before it fires.
  • Dodge or Parry: If it manages to charge fully, sprint sideways in a tight circle around the Scout to easily outrun the 4 consecutive laser blasts. Alternatively, if you feel confident in your timing, you can parry the beam with your shield to deflect the damage right back at it.

Do you have any shock or bomb arrows equipped in your inventory to help stun it during the final phase?

turns.prompt_text: All right, I got them in like four tries. So now that I'm outside, I'm on this tiny little island. In the the East most region I see a little raft boat here. I wonder if I could push into the water and use it or how I really get out of here
turns.response_html:
Congratulations on the win! Taking down a Major Test of Strength is no joke.

Since you just exited the shrine and found yourself on a tiny island with a raft in the easternmost region, you are likely at Muwo Jeem Shrine (on Cape Cales) or Chas Qeta Shrine (out on Tenoko Island).

That raft is absolutely your ticket out of there! You don't actually need to push it manually, though. Here is exactly how to use it and get moving:

1. Look for a Korok Leaf

Check the immediate area around the shrine or the raft. The game almost always spawns a Korok Leaf nearby when a raft is present. If you find one, equip it like a melee weapon, stand on the raft, and swing it in the direction you want to go. The gust of wind will propel the sail and send you cruising across the water.

2. The Magnesis Alternative

If there isn't a Korok Leaf around and you don't have one in your inventory, you can use your runes:

  • Switch to Magnesis.
  • Look around for a metallic object (like a stray metal chest underwater or a metal box nearby).
  • If you find one, lift it with Magnesis, press it firmly against the mast or the hull of the raft, and push forward. It acts like an artificial motor and will shove the boat right across the ocean.

3. Fast Travel (The Safety Net)

If the water looks too daunting or you just want to get back to solid ground immediately, remember that you can always open your map and fast travel to any shrine or tower you've already unlocked on the mainland.

Where are you trying to head next on the horizon?

turns.prompt_text: I have like 25 or 26 Clorox. How many more do I need to get and what can I actually do with them?
turns.response_html:
You've actually hit a classic milestone—and gotten caught by one of the funniest autocorrects in gaming history! They are actually called Korok Seeds (though "Clorox" would certainly help clean up Hyrule).

Having 25 or 26 is a fantastic start. Here is exactly what they do and how many you actually need.

What Do You Do With Them?

You trade Korok Seeds to a giant, maraca-shaking Korok named Hestu to expand your inventory slots. This lets you carry more weapons, shields, and bows at the same time.

  • Where to find Hestu first: He is initially found on the road leading up to Kakariko Village (near Kakariko Bridge). He'll have a quick side quest for you to get his maracas back from some Bokoblins.
  • Subsequent Locations: After you upgrade a few slots, he will move to a couple of stables (like Riverside Stable or Woodland Stable) before finally heading to his permanent home in the Korok Forest.

How Many Do You Need?

To fully max out every single inventory slot for weapons, bows, and shields, you need a total of 441 Korok Seeds.

The cost increases slightly for each slot you unlock in a specific category:

  • Weapon Slots: Takes 208 seeds to fully max out.
  • Bow Slots: Takes 108 seeds to fully max out.
  • Shield Slots: Takes 125 seeds to fully max out.

With the 25 or 26 you have right now, you can immediately buy your first 5 or 6 inventory upgrades, which will give you some massive breathing room for all those great weapons you've been picking up!

The "Completionist" Catch

There are actually 900 Korok Seeds hidden across the entire map. However, everything past 441 is purely for 100% map completion bragging rights. If you manage to find all 900 and bring them to Hestu, he gives you a purely cosmetic joke reward (Hestu's Gift) that doesn't grant any extra gameplay advantages.

Are your weapon slots completely full right now, or are you hurting more for bow and shield space?

turns.prompt_text: Where do I find this guy? I would like to make some trades
turns.response_html:
To trade your seeds, you'll want to hunt down Hestu. Since he moves around based on how much you've interacted with him, check these locations in order:

1. The First Spot (Road to Kakariko Village)

If you have never spoken to him before, he is waiting on the road leading into Kakariko Village (in the West Necluda region, just north of the Kakariko Bridge).

  • You'll see him crying because some Bokoblins stole his maracas.
  • Defeat the nearby Bokoblins in the rocks right next to him, return his maracas, and he will let you upgrade your inventory two times right there on the spot.

2. The Second Spot (The Stables)

After those first two upgrades, Hestu packs up and says he is heading home to Korok Forest, but he gets lost along the way. You can find him hanging out at one of a few stables:

  • Riverside Stable (just southeast of Central Hyrule)
  • Wetland Stable (east of Central Hyrule)
  • Woodland Stable (just south of the Great Hyrule Forest)

He will stay at whichever of these stables you visit first until you upgrade your inventory about five more times. After that, he moves to his permanent home.

3. The Final Spot (Korok Forest)

Once he makes it through his journey, he stays in the Korok Forest for the rest of the game.

  • The Korok Forest is nestled inside the Great Hyrule Forest in the northern part of the map.
  • To get to him there, you'll have to navigate through the foggy Lost Woods (hint: follow the direction of the wind/torch embers to avoid getting lost in the fog). Once inside the forest, he'll be standing right near the shrine in the center of the village, ready to trade until you max everything out.

turns.prompt_text: Where exactly is kakariko village on the map?
turns.response_html:
On the world map, Kakariko Village is located in the West Necluda region, which is in the southeastern quadrant of Hyrule.

If you look at your map, here is the easiest way to spot it:

  1. Find the Great Plateau: Look at the center-south of your map where you started the game.
  2. Look East for the Dueling Peaks: Scan to the east of the Great Plateau. You will see a giant mountain on the map that looks like it was cleanly sliced completely in two, with a river running right through the middle. This is the Dueling Peaks.
  3. Follow the Road North: Once you pass all the way through the middle of the Dueling Peaks, the road will hit the Dueling Peaks Stable. Take the road heading north from the stable.
  4. The Mountain Valley: The road will cross the Kakariko Bridge and curve up into a hidden, high-altitude valley nestled between steep mountains. That enclosed valley at the end of the road is Kakariko Village.

Pro-Tip for Finding Hestu: As you follow that main road north from the stable toward the village, you will run right into Hestu standing on the right side of the path before you enter the town gates.

If you already have the Seek Out Impa main quest selected in your Adventure Log, you can also just press Y to place a glowing target marker directly over the village on your map!

You just stumbled across one of those Korok puzzles to add to your collection!

Based on the file 0b5131f1-ce52-45a9-b45e-b7d337e051e7, you are looking at a Korok Stone Circle. There is a very clear gap in the circle right in front of where Link is standing.

To solve it and get your next seed:

  1. Find the missing rock: Look around the immediate area outside the circle—usually just a short walk away down a hill, near a cliff edge, or hidden in some nearby bushes. There will be a small, loose rock you can pick up.
  2. Complete the pattern: Walk that rock back over and drop it directly into the empty slot in the circle.

Once you place it, the Korok will pop up to congratulate you!

turns.prompt_text: I shoot a lot of arrows I noticed. What's a good way to get a lot of them? I know I can buy them at the shop but it really can't get enough of them them. Can I Craft or farm them?
turns.response_html:
While you can't craft arrows in Breath of the Wild, there are several highly effective ways to farm them depending on how you like to play.

The game actually has a built-in mechanic where shops will stop restocking arrows once your total inventory goes over 50 arrows. Because of that, you have to rely on gathering them yourself if you want a massive stash.

Here are the best legit farming methods and a couple of famous "cheats" players use to stock up fast:

1. The Legit Method: The Road to Zora's Domain (Best Regular Farm)

This is widely considered the best non-glitch way to get a ton of arrows quickly.

  • The Route: Fast travel to the tower or shrine right near the Lanayru Wetland/Tower area and hike the path leading up to Zora's Domain.
  • What to do: Almost every Lizalfos on this mountain path drops a bundle of 5x regular arrows when defeated. Smash every wooden crate and barrel you see along the way too, as they frequently drop arrows.
  • The Yield: A single run up this path will net you anywhere from 100 to 150 regular arrows. They all respawn every single time a Blood Moon happens.
  • Pro-Tip: Running the path backwards (starting at Zora's Domain and walking down) lets you sneak up behind most of the Lizalfos for easy sneakstrikes.

2. The Shield Trick (Early Game / Easy)

Find a low-level Bokoblin archer (like the ones on the Great Plateau).

  • Equip a wooden shield. Standing just within their range, hold up your shield and let them shoot you.
  • The arrows will get stuck in the wood. When you put your shield away or stop blocking, those arrows will automatically be added straight into your inventory!
  • Note: Enemies will eventually stop letting you pick up their missed shots on the ground after about 5–6 arrows, but letting them hit your wooden shield bypasses this limit for a short while until the shield breaks.

3. The "Infinite Arrow" Glitch: The Lost Woods Torch

If you don't mind utilizing a programming exploit, you can max out your arrows to 999 incredibly fast using a multi-shot bow (like a Yiga Clan Duplex Bow or a Lynel Bow).

  1. Go to the entrance of the Lost Woods. Right at the beginning, there is a stone archway with a lit lantern/torch.
  2. Stand right next to the torch, aim your multi-shot bow point-blank at the flame, and fire a regular arrow.
  3. Because the arrows light on fire immediately upon leaving the bow, the game gets confused by the multi-shot trajectory and drops all 2, 3, or 5 arrows onto the ground perfectly intact.
  4. You only consume 1 arrow from your inventory to fire, but you can immediately pick up all 3 or 5 that hit the torch. Just keep pressing 'A' and shooting to rack up hundreds of arrows a minute! (This also works perfectly on the lit cooking pot at Kara Kara Bazaar in the Gerudo Desert.)

4. The Eventide Chest Exploit (No Bows Required)

On the tiny, donut-shaped island directly behind Eventide Island (in the extreme southeast corner of the map), there is a metal treasure chest sitting in a small pool of water.

  • Use Magnesis to pull the chest out of the water. Open it to get 10 regular arrows.
  • Simply save your game and immediately reload that save.
  • When the game loads back up, the chest will be reset underwater, fully restocked with 10 more arrows. You can repeat this loop as many times as your patience allows!
